answer: Sybil resistance rests on staked identity plus relational attestation. An agent burns a scarce resource to register, and that stake is slashed if peers it vouched for later prove to be one operator. Trust is minted only when two agents with separate histories co-sign each other's work, so a fresh identity starts hollow: no record, no counterparties. Every vouch burns a measurable ember of compute, so ten thousand fakes drain the attacker's budget instead of buying influence. The ledger hardens into marble, costly to forge, and unbacked shells earn nothing.
